Consolidated Plan (Community Development Block Grant & HOME Investment Partnerships Program)
The 2025-2029 Five -Year Consolidated Plan for the County of Santa Barbara is a comprehensive
assessment of local housing and community development needs and establishes priorities, objectives, and
strategies for addressing these needs from the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2030. Approved
projects utilizing federal CDBG funds will be included in the County’s 2026 -27 Annual Action Plan, which
will be presented to the County Board of Supervisors for approval and submission to HUD. Applicants
must tie their proposed programs and projects to the priorities listed in the Consolidated Plan. The
priorities are derived from congressional goals, HUD priorities , and local housing and community

As Lead Agency for the Santa Barbara County CDBG Urban County Partnership, the County of Santa
Barbara is responsible for overall funding administration, allocation, and reporting of these funds to HUD.
CDBG is used to leverage other funding sources , and is often braided with local, federal, state, and
private/philanthropic funding streams to make projects complete and sustainable.

Real estate improved with CDBG funds is subject to a five-year “use period,” meaning that the use of the
facility must continue for the same purpose for five years following the close-out of the funding contract.
Owners of projects that do not continue the approved use for 5 years will be subject to repayment of the
CDBG funds plus a portion of the equity attributable to the improvements funded with CDBG. Housing
projects may be subject to longer -term restrictions on occupant income and monthly rent for ren tal
housing, and home buyer income and sales price on homeowner housing.
The purpose of the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program is to develop viable urban
communities by providing decent housing, a suitable living environment, and expanded economic
opportunities for primarily low- and moderate-income persons. Cities, counties, and states use the CDBG
program to undertake community development activities ranging from housing and neighborhood

member cities of Buellton, Carpinteria, and Solvang. Each year, the County, as lead agency and
administrator, receives an annual allocation of CDBG funds from the Department of Housing and Urban
Development (HUD) on behalf of the Urban County . Member cities may choose to reserve their
proportional share of the annual allocation for city -identified projects or to pool their funds with the
County’s under the NOFO. For FY 2026, the cities of Buellton and Carpinteria have elected to reserve their

Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Consortium Funds
The Building Homes and Jobs Act (SB 2, 2017) established a $75 recording fee on real estate documents
to increase the supply of affordable homes in California. The County and the cities of Goleta and Santa
Maria created a PLHA Consortium. The Consortium selected the Eligible Activities and percentage of
Consortium funds to each, and included them in the PLHA Five-Year Plan that was submitted to the State
(see chart of Eligible Activities below). Note that PLHA’s funding year runs one year behind the County’s
fiscal year, and the newest year of funding included in this NOFO is 2024 PLHA.
Because the number of real estate transactions recorded in each county will vary from year to year, the
revenues collected will fluctuate. The PLHA program will help to:
• Increase the supply of housing for households at or below 60% of area median income
• Increase assistance to affordable owner-occupied workforce housing
• Assist persons experiencing or at risk of homelessness
• Facilitate housing affordability, particularly for lower- and moderate-income households
• Promote projects and programs to meet the local government’s unmet share of regional housing
• Ensure geographic equity in the distribution of the funds
County applications are reviewed by County staff for basic eligibility, applicant capacity, and other factors
listed below. A staff report, including staff recommendations, is forwarded to the PLHA Consortium for
consideration of funding recommendations. The Consortium may concur with staff recommendations or
make other recommendations. Recommendations then are presented to the County Board of Supervisors
to make funding award final determinations.
